message.content:
Below is a list of **federal holidays in Canada that create long weekends** in 2023.  
(If you’re planning for a specific province, note that many provinces have additional holidays that also generate long weekends—see the “Provincial notes” section.)

| Date | Holiday | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span |
|------|---------|-------------|-------------------|
| Jan 1 2023 | New Year’s Day | Sunday | Sat Dec 31 2022 – Sun Jan 1 2023 |
| Feb 20 2023 | Family Day (BC, AB, ON, SK, NB, PE) | Monday | Sat Feb 18 2023 – Mon Feb 20 2023 |
| Apr 7 2023 | Good Friday | Friday | Fri Apr 7 2023 – Sun Apr 9 2023 |
| May 22 2023 | Victoria Day | Monday | Sat May 20 2023 – Mon May 22 2023 |
| Jul 1 2023 | Canada Day | Saturday | Sat Jul 1 2023 – Sun Jul 2 2023 |
| Sep 4 2023 | Labour Day | Monday | Sat Sep 2 2023 – Mon Sep 4 2023 |
| Oct 9 2023 | Thanksgiving | Monday | Sat Oct 7 2023 – Mon Oct 9 2023 |
| Nov 11 2023 | Remembrance Day | Saturday | Sat Nov 11 2023 – Sun Nov 12 2023 |
| Dec 25 2023 | Christmas Day | Monday | Sat Dec 23 2023 – Mon Dec 25 2023 |

### Provincial notes
- **Civic Holiday** (first Monday in August) is observed in most provinces (except BC, AB, ON, PE, NB, SK, and NL) and creates a long weekend on that Monday.
- **Family Day** dates vary by province; the above date applies to BC, AB, ON, SK, NB, and PE. Other provinces have different holidays on the same day (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in PE, Louis Riel Day in MB, etc.).
- **Boxing Day** (Dec 26) is a federal holiday but falls on a Tuesday in 2023, so it does **not** create a long weekend unless combined with Christmas (which it does not in this year).

Feel free to let me know if you need the long‑weekend list for a particular province or any other details!
